questions.question: Race is described by scientists as a social construct because:
options: It is decided by a person's DNA alone
Its categories were created by societies, not by natural biological divisions
It does not affect anyone's life
Only a few countries use it

questions.question: Prejudice means:
options: Forming an opinion about someone before knowing the facts

questions.question: Refusing someone a job because of their race is an example of:
options: Prejudice that stays only in the mind

questions.question: Why do many writers say racism is most harmful when combined with power?
options: Because power lets racist beliefs shape laws, jobs, land and education
Because powerless people cannot have opinions

questions.question: The modern idea of ranked races developed mainly alongside:
options: The invention of the printing press
European colonialism and the Atlantic slave trade

questions.question: Scientific racism was:
options: Careful science that proved racial superiority
Flawed pseudo-science used to rank races and justify domination

questions.question: Sarah Baartman's remains were returned to South Africa for burial in:
Why did racist ideas grow alongside slavery?
options: They were used to justify treating people as property

questions.question: Racism built into a society's laws and institutions is called:
Which apartheid law classified every South African by race?
Hostility towards foreigners, such as attacks on African migrants in 2008, is called:
Why can institutional racism continue after racist laws are repealed?
options: Because new racist laws are always passed
Because inequalities created over decades remain in wealth, land and education

subtopics.title: Challenging Racism Today, and the Error Museum

questions.question: A founding value of South Africa's Constitution is:
Which section of the Bill of Rights deals with equality?
Which statement is correct?
options: Human races are separate biological types
Racism is natural and cannot change
Racism is learnt, so it can be unlearnt

questions.question: Which is a good response to a racist joke at school?
options: Refuse to join in and calmly say it is not okay, if it is safe
Ignore the person who was targeted

questions.question: The "boxes" in the Simplifier story are:
options: Racial categories people were sorted into

questions.question: Skin colour changed over thousands of years mainly because of:
options: The amount of sunlight where people's ancestors lived

questions.question: A stereotype is:
options: A fixed idea that everyone in a group is the same

questions.question: In the Simplifier story, the "lie that paid well" was:
options: That Africans were less than fully human, used to justify slavery

questions.question: Sarah Baartman was a:
After World War II, scientists:
options: Rejected the idea of superior races

questions.question: Why was scientific racism called bad science?
options: Its conclusions were decided in advance and its methods were flawed

questions.question: In the football picture, institutional racism is like:
options: Unfair rules that favour one team

questions.question: Under apartheid, your race decided:
options: Where you could live, study, work and whether you could vote

questions.question: Why is South Africa still very unequal today?
options: Because decades of unfair rules left a lasting gap

questions.question: What is the main idea of this lesson?
options: Races are natural ranks of people
Racism is a learnt, false belief in superior races that can be challenged
Racism only exists in South Africa
